ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within a grid formed by small squares, the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all lattice points (intersections of the grid lines). What is the value of $\tan\angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, draw AD$\perp$BC at D. \\
In $\triangle ABD$, $\tan\angle ABC=\frac{AD}{BD}=\frac{1}{2}$, \\
thus, $\tan\angle ABC=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC on a square grid. Points B and C lie on the same horizontal grid line, so BC is horizontal. From B to the vertical grid line through A, there are 4 small-square widths to the right. From B up to A, there are 2 small-square heights. Reasoning: Angle ABC is the angle between BA and the horizontal ray BC. Therefore tan(angle ABC) equals rise over run for segment BA, which is 2/4 = 1/2.
